title: Randomized Trial of Behavior Therapy for Adults With Tourette Syndrome
publication_date_type: August 2012 journal issue dated August 1; no earlier online-first date verified
newness: Historical 2012 trial analyzed on 15 October 2026; not new-window evidence. PMC author manuscript available 13 September 2013.
design: Three-site masked-assessor randomized ten-week CBIT versus psychoeducation/supportive therapy (PST); response-conditioned follow-up with offered monthly boosters. PST nonresponders could cross to CBIT.
population: Ages 16–69; adult-dominant, not adult-only. TS/chronic tic disorders with at least moderate severity. Six screened with TTS above 30 received panel review; three enrolled and three excluded. Stable medication/comorbidity and English/IQ criteria limit severe/unstable-adult extrapolation.
primary_endpoint: Week-10 tic severity; categorical CGI-I response (1 or 2) separately reported. Impairment is a registry secondary endpoint.
key_result: Published adjusted acute YGTSS-TTS advantage 3.3 points (95% CI 1.4–5.2), p<.001; impairment advantage 3.9 (0.5–7.2), p=.03 without secondary multiplicity adjustment. Six-month CGI-I positive: CBIT 12/15 assessed versus 12/24 all acute responders; PST 1/2 assessed versus 1/4 acute responders.
uncertainty: Continuous model requires a postrandomization visit and MAR; response-selected and incomplete follow-up, booster-inclusive protocol, unverified actual booster attendance, and control crossover prevent a causal all-randomized six-month comparison. No direct original-report follow-up impairment/GTS-QOL effect or adult-only estimate.
negative_findings: Medication/severity moderator nulls do not establish equivalence. Nine of 24 CBIT acute responders and two of four PST responders have unknown follow-up outcomes.
reporting_discrepancies: Abstract PST 4/63(6.4%) conflicts with body/allocation 4/59(6.8%); six-month prose mixes denominators. Reported NNT5 is not reproduced by reciprocal raw CGI risk difference3.1933 (ceiling4). Author-manuscript and final-published impairment/medication percentages differ.
safety: 224 adverse events and three serious events judged unlikely related; tic worsening in four participants per arm. Event totals differ from affected-person counts; rare or long-term harm not excluded.
funding_conflicts: NIMH and Tourette Syndrome Association support; treatment-manual royalties, professional honoraria and other relationships disclosed; sponsor role declared absent.
inference_not_supported: 80% all-randomized six-month response, continuous remission, adult-only efficacy, off-treatment durability, causal long-term superiority, QoL surrogacy, disease modification or cure.
reproducible_analysis: Exact finite-cohort enumeration gives six-month CBIT acute-responder maintenance bounds 50–87.5%, with 62.5% follow-up ascertainment; not confidence intervals. 37 implementation checks plus 49 independent comparison checks passed; output reproduced exactly.
retrieval_status: Final JAMA HTML, PubMed, current official registry API, one readable PMC manuscript fetch and visually inspected PMC flow diagram. No full papers or figures included in deliverables.
correction_retraction_check: None identified in bounded exact-title/DOI searches and inspected PubMed record; not comprehensive clearance.
next_verification_task: Audit same-trial McGuire secondary functioning report (PMID31451122; online2019-08-27, issue2020-09): randomized acute disability/social/family effects versus responder associations and selected follow-up; retain denominators, instrument direction, uncertainty, multiplicity and null findings.
